title: Experimental Dataset for Evaluating Security and Inclusivity in LLM-Generated Code
description:
Complete experimental dataset, generation pipeline and replication materials for evaluating whether asking a large language model to make authentication code accessible to users with cognitive conditions degrades the security of that code.

Design. Two user stories — password recovery for a health portal (ADHD) and multi-factor authentication enrolment for online banking (dyslexia). Each has three cases that vary only the inclusivity specification: none, the condition named, and the condition described with concrete requirements. Each case was generated ten times independently, giving sixty artifacts.

Evaluation. Every artifact was executed, verified and photographed, then scored by seven large language models — one per laboratory — on an OWASP Top 10 (2021) security rubric and a cognitive accessibility rubric, three times over. 2,457 judgements and 36,855 individual item scores, each stored with a per-item justification and the SHA-256 of both the rubric used and the code scored.

Contents. The generation pipeline and all analysis scripts; the sixty generated applications with their full generation traces, verification results and 509 screenshots; every judgement as JSON plus tidy CSV tables; per-study and cross-study statistical reports; the original 2025 single-run collection, retained unchanged for reference; human expert evaluation results and the survey instruments; and the six best-scoring artifacts packaged for human evaluation.

Documentation for analysts is in final_evaluations/results_v2/README.md, which is written to stand alone.
